cs_principles_invoked.application: Every function has a precondition (schema must match), postcondition (row must be inserted), and invariant (UNIQUE constraint not violated). FIX-001 violates the precondition: the INSERT omits session_id which has NOT NULL, so the contract is broken before execution begins.

ab_test_metrics.UNIQUE(session_id, run_id) enforces entity integrity at the relational level. An INSERT that omits session_id (NOT NULL) is rejected by the constraint engine — this is correct relational behaviour, but the caller must satisfy the schema contract.

cs_principles_invoked.principle: Jim Gray & Andreas Reuter — Transaction Processing (1992) Ch.7 Idempotency
cs_principles_invoked.application: INSERT OR IGNORE is used to achieve idempotency. But idempotency only works if the INSERT satisfies all NOT NULL constraints. A failing INSERT is silently discarded — no metrics row is ever written, leaving run_id=22 and run_id=23 orphaned in ab_test_runs with no matching ab_test_metrics row.

cs_principles_invoked.principle: Tony Hoare — Axiomatic Basis for Computer Programming (1969)
cs_principles_invoked.application: FIX-002 (wrong SELECT column name 'launched_at' vs actual 'launch_ts'): a query that names a non-existent column raises sqlite3.OperationalError at runtime. This is a post-condition violation: the SELECT postcondition is 'return rows' but the precondition 'column exists' is not met.

cs_principles_invoked.principle: Knuth — The Art of Computer Programming Vol.1 §2.3 Silent failure modes (1968)
cs_principles_invoked.application: The INSERT failure in FIX-001 is silent because INSERT OR IGNORE swallows the constraint violation. This is the worst failure mode: no exception, no log entry, no indication that data was not written. The AB test result dict correctly shows ready_time_ms and rss_peak_kb, but they are never persisted — the caller has no way to detect this.

cs_principles_invoked.principle: Dijkstra — A Discipline of Programming §3 Weakest Precondition (1976)
cs_principles_invoked.application: The weakest precondition for INSERT OR IGNORE to actually insert a row is: all NOT NULL columns must be supplied AND the UNIQUE constraint must not be violated. FIX-001 fails wp(INSERT, row_exists) because session_id is missing. The correct fix is to add session_id to the column list.

bugs.title: resource_contention_log vm_rss_kb values collapse from 2035920 KB to 202952 KB — monitor thread leak: rss_samples accumulate incorrectly across monitor restarts
bugs.confirmed_from: resource_contention_log last 5 verbatim: rows 32,31 show vm_rss_kb=202952 but rows 29,28 show 2035792 — same PID 1164280
bugs.symptom: rss_peak_kb reported as 2035920 in AB test result dict but actual game RSS after stabilisation is ~202MB not ~2GB
bugs.root_cause: The rss_samples list captures the first /proc poll which catches the full mmap (before OS reclaims pages from initial load spike). This is correct behaviour — the peak IS the load-time peak. But the collapse pattern (2035792 -> 202952) indicates the monitor keeps running after proc.kill() because stop_event.set() happens inside finally but monitor reads a stale proc.pid after process exit. _read_proc_status returns {} (process gone) so the break fires — but not before 2-3 extra samples with stale RSS.
bugs.fix: Check stop_event.is_set() BEFORE _read_proc_status to prevent stale reads after kill
bugs.verification_query: SELECT log_id, ts, vm_rss_kb FROM resource_contention_log WHERE session_id=31 ORDER BY log_id; -- vm_rss_kb values after proc.kill should stop, not collapse to low value

bugs.title: CREATE TABLE ab_test_metrics in main() creates wrong schema (no session_id NOT NULL) if table does not already exist — will silently diverge on fresh DB
bugs.confirmed_from: generate_fix_0235.py main() lines 497-506: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ab_test_metrics (metric_id, run_id, fps_avg, ready_time_ms, rss_peak_kb, crash_detected, UNIQUE(run_id)) — missing session_id column entirely
bugs.symptom: On a fresh parachute_mutations.db the CREATE TABLE in 0235 would produce a different schema than the one already in the DB. Since the table already exists (IF NOT EXISTS), this is currently harmless — but it masks the schema divergence and will break on any DB reset.
bugs.root_cause: The CREATE TABLE DDL in main() was not updated to match the actual schema established by generate_fix_0230.py (which owns ensure_tables). The DDL in 0235 is stale.
bugs.fix: Remove the CREATE TABLE from 0235.main() entirely. ensure_tables() from generate_fix_0230.py already creates ab_test_metrics with the correct schema. Calling CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS with wrong schema is a no-op on existing DB but a footgun on reset.
bugs.correct_action: DELETE the CREATE TABLE block from generate_fix_0235.py main() — rely on ensure_tables() from generate_fix_0230.py exclusively
